Justin Jincaid

GNGM

Hunter

📌

Google just launched Playground, and this looks pretty fun. You can describe a game idea in plain English, and Google's AI turns it into something you can actually play in your browser. Want to change the rules, characters, or physics? Just ask. You can also share your games, publish them for others to play, and even create multiplayer experiences. The interesting part is that Google is also working with Unity to bring more advanced game creation into Playground. Curious to see what people come up with when making a game becomes this easy.

Google Playground is an experimental AI gaming platform that lets anyone create, play, and share custom games without coding. Describe your idea, choose a genre, and let AI build a playable game in minutes. Change the rules, characters, physics, or visuals simply by chatting. Share your creation with friends, publish it to the community gallery, or explore games made by others. Powered by Google's Gemini, Nano Banana, and Lyria models.

results.title: Google Mixboard 2.0: Now w/ Nano Banana Pro, new file types & multi-board project | Product Hunt
results.content:
Rohan Chaubey

Hunter

📌

Super excited to share a big Mixboard update with you all!

Mixboard has always been a playground for ideas and this release makes it even more powerful.

Google has introduced a bundle of updates to help you keep exploring your ideas: [...] Nano Banana Pro: You can now turn your boards directly into presentations using Nano Banana Pro, Google's latest Gemini image model. Better visuals, smarter layouts, and a way faster path from concept to something you can actually share.
 New File Types: They have also added support for new file types (including PDFs, HEIC & TIFF), a built-in selfie camera, and even doodle-based editing for more control over your visuals.
 Multi-Board Projects: For bigger projects, you can now work across multiple boards within one project, giving you space to separate brainstorming, exploration and final vision.

& more!
